root_cause.text: The partial overlap detection for start elements in anonymous sets was entirely skipped, allowing insertion of overlapping intervals where a new start element falls within an existing interval (i.e., the previous element is an end element), violating interval semantics.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies the condition in `__nft_rbtree_insert` to add a check: after verifying `rbe_le` and `nft_rbtree_interval_start(rbe_le)` and `nft_rbtree_interval_start(new)`, if the set is anonymous, it now checks whether the previous active element (`rbe_prev`) is an end element; if so, it returns `-ENOTEMPTY`. The commit message explicitly states that the previous logic skipped anonymous set checks for start elements incorrectly, allowing overlap like A-B and A-C with C < B.
